overview: South Africa has one of Africa's most developed health-tech ecosystems and a mature market for sexual and reproductive health, anchored by the government's flagship MomConnect maternal mHealth service and a heavy public HIV/SRH burden concentrated among young women. Its femtech startup scene remains small but growing, led by Johannesburg's Zoie Health, while gender-lens funds and continental platforms such as UNICEF Femtech Ventures increasingly target the country. Landmark policy shifts, including the 2024 National Health Insurance Act and a national SRHR policy, are reshaping how women's health is financed and delivered.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent developments span funding platforms, HIV prevention finance, and encouraging shifts in adolescent and maternal health data.

items.text: UNICEF Femtech Ventures activated its first cohort of 11 startups (from 1,100+ applications across 85 countries), convened in Pretoria, each receiving up to USD 100,000 equity-free.
Public-sector data showed teen pregnancies dropped 16 percent across all nine provinces between April 2021 and March 2025, with births to girls aged 10 to 14 falling nearly 40 percent.
Five35 Ventures, a female-focused pan-African VC and Kasha co-investor, secured an anchor investment from the Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund to expand its women-focused portfolio.
The Global Fund, with PEPFAR, CIFF and the Gates Foundation, moved to roll out twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir HIV prevention for around 2 million people, a priority for young women.
A US executive order froze PEPFAR funding (roughly USD 400M+/year to SA HIV programmes) for a 90-day review; adolescent girls and women flagged among the first affected.
Reporting highlighted that women-led African health-tech firms, including SA's Zoie Health, secured USD 52M in funding, a 2,000 percent-plus increase.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: South Africa combines one of the world's most liberal abortion laws with an ambitious universal-coverage and digital-health agenda.

items.text: President Ramaphosa signed the National Health Insurance (NHI) Act No. 20 of 2023 into law, launching a phased path to universal health coverage with women cited as direct beneficiaries.
The National Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) Policy, Edition 1, set a rights-based framework covering contraception, fertility treatment and safe abortion care.
The National Digital Health Strategy for South Africa 2019-2024 set a vision of better health enabled by digital health, prioritising scale-up of mHealth like MomConnect.
Revised National Contraception Clinical Guidelines expanded the method mix, including the Implanon NXT subdermal implant and the female condom.
The Choice on Termination of Pregnancy Act legalised abortion on request up to 12 weeks, among the most liberal abortion laws globally; clinical guideline last updated 2021.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: New funds, catalytic platforms and government digital-health rollouts are reshaping the women's health landscape.

items.text: UNICEF Femtech Ventures, a five-year (2025-2030) platform backed by Sweden and Temasek Foundation, hosted its inaugural cohort in Pretoria, offering up to USD 100,000 equity-free per startup.
SA impact investor E Squared deployed over R300M into startups in 2025 (R1.37bn lifetime across 227 ventures), including femtech via its Zoie Health participation.
The SAMRC and PATH launched a Global Health Innovation Accelerator (GHIA) for medical devices, diagnostics and tools serving vulnerable women and children.
Startupbootcamp AfriTech co-runs a USD 7M healthtech project (with Salient Advisory and SCIDaR), supported by the Gates Foundation, backing African digital-health startups.
The National Department of Health began beta rollout of the e-Impilo national electronic medical record in primary care facilities in 2025, using biometric patient identification.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Disclosed femtech rounds remain scarce; Kasha's SA-expansion Series B is the largest, with most local deals undisclosed pre-seed rounds or equity-free grants.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The ecosystem spans a handful of femtech startups, government mHealth programmes, world-class research institutes and major SRH NGOs.

items.name: Zoie Health
items.note: Johannesburg Black woman-led digital women's health clinic: virtual consults, medication subscriptions, family planning, fertility and maternity

items.name: Kasha
items.note: Women-focused digital retail and last-mile delivery of sanitary products, contraceptives and pharmaceuticals; operates in South Africa

items.name: Aviro Health
items.note: Cape Town healthtech; Aviro Pocket Clinic offers digital HIV and SRH counselling and decision-support for providers

items.name: Femmflo
items.note: South Africa's first hormone and mental-health app with in-lab and at-home testing

items.name: Oky South Africa
items.note: Period-tracking app for young girls, launched by loveLife and UNICEF; zero-rated and multilingual

items.name: MomConnect (Dept of Health)
items.note: National maternal mHealth service via SMS and WhatsApp in all 11 official languages; ~4.7M mothers registered

items.name: National Department of Health
items.note: Runs SRHR policy, MomConnect, HPV vaccination and Saving Mothers confidential enquiries

items.name: Wits RHI
items.note: Wits Reproductive Health and HIV Institute; leading African research institute on HIV, SRH and PrEP trials across all nine provinces

items.name: SAMRC
items.note: South African Medical Research Council; largest local health-research funder with a Gender and Health Research Unit

items.name: MSI Reproductive Choices South Africa
items.note: Largest non-profit provider of abortion and SRH care in South Africa (formerly Marie Stopes)

items.name: loveLife
items.note: Youth SRH/HIV NGO (founded 1999) reducing new HIV infections and unplanned pregnancies among 15-24 year-olds

items.name: Startupbootcamp AfriTech
items.note: Cape Town pan-African accelerator with a healthtech track and Gates-supported digital-health programme

items.name: Founders Factory Africa
items.note: Johannesburg early-stage investor and accelerator with a broad healthtech portfolio; USD 114M raised

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Gender-lens funds, impact investors and multilateral financiers underpin SA's women's health and femtech activity.

items.name: Enygma Ventures
items.role: First VC fund solely for female entrepreneurs in the SADC region; invested USD 3.5M across 10 businesses including in South Africa

items.name: 4DX Ventures
items.role: Led Zoie Health's pre-seed extension round

items.name: E Squared Investments
items.role: Impact investor (Allan Gray); participated in Zoie Health pre-seed extension; R300M+ deployed in 2025

items.name: Knife Capital
items.role: Led Kasha's USD 21M Series B funding SA expansion of women's health commerce

items.name: Five35 Ventures
items.role: Female-focused seed/Series A VC; Kasha co-investor; anchored by Mastercard Foundation in 2025

items.name: Dazzle Angels
items.role: First female-focused angel network in SA; interests include healthcare and maternal/child health

items.name: Global Fund
items.role: Major multilateral financier of SA HIV programmes; co-funding injectable lenacapavir rollout

items.name: PEPFAR (US)
items.role: Bilateral funder of SA HIV programmes (~USD 400M+/year); funding under review from Jan 2025

items.name: Gates Foundation
items.role: Co-funds lenacapavir HIV rollout and backs the SBC AfriTech healthtech project
